description: We are CURIE-X, a team of Computer Engineering, Chemical Engineering and Law-Finance Students who have solid experience developing applications using technologies like Python (FASTAPI) and JavaScript (React) to build AI-powered digital experiences to solve complex problems.
summary:
FireGuard AI is a multilingual platform built for NASA’s Flame in Freefall challenge, unifying 3,798 microgravity combustion experiments across 12 orbital investigations (including BASS, ACME BRE, CFI-G, FLEX, and Saffire). It integrates a machine learning flammability risk model, a Lunar (0.166g) and Martian (0.38g) physics scaling engine, a camera-controlled 3D flame simulator using hand-tracking gestures, and Curie, a voice-activated chatbot ("Hey Curie") powered by the Gemini API and RAG across all NASA flight investigations—allowing researchers, professors, and students in chemistry, physics, mathematics, and aerospace engineering to query findings without manually digging through repositories while citing exact data sources to prevent bias.Without buoyant convection, space fires form spherical, diffusion-limited, and nearly invisible cool flames that invalidate terrestrial safety codes.

 FireGuard AI addresses this by turning fragmented orbital data into validated flammability boundaries, risk scores, and interactive simulations. Because fire is a catastrophic hazard in crewed spaceflight, these predictive and smoke-detection insights help engineers protect astronauts on future Artemis and deep-space missions.
details:
FireGuard AI is a full-stack scientific platform built to transform fragmented NASA microgravity combustion records into actionable fire-safety intelligence. By consolidating 3,798 experimental records from 12 orbital investigations (including BASS, ACME BRE, CFI-G, FLEX, and Saffire) alongside 24 peer-reviewed NASA research papers, the platform connects three core analytical modules into a single workflow. First, a machine learning flammability risk model predicts material ignition limits and computes real-time risk scores across custom atmospheric compositions, while a physics-based scaling engine extrapolates zero-gravity flight baselines to simulate fire behavior under Lunar (0.166g) and Martian (0.38g) gravity levels. Second, an interactive 3D flame simulator uses browser-based computer vision and webcam hand-tracking so users can rotate, zoom, and inspect spherical, diffusion-limited flames and smoke dispersion with natural hand gestures. Third, Curie—our multilingual voice and text chatbot activated by saying "Hey Curie"—uses the Google Gemini API and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over a hybrid PostgreSQL database (combining vector search and full-text indexing across more than 80,000 lines of NASA literature) to answer scientific queries while citing exact primary sources to eliminate bias and manual repository searches.

To engineer this architecture, we combined a modern web frontend built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript—integrating real-time 3D rendering, webcam hand-tracking, the Web Speech API for wake-word detection, and multi-language internationalization—with a high-performance Python and FastAPI backend. Our data science and modeling pipeline leverages Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn for dataset harmonization, feature engineering, flammability risk prediction, and partial-gravity physics scaling, backed by PostgreSQL with hybrid vector/full-text search and the Gemini API for source-grounded explanations.

Rather than building a conventional static dashboard, our team prioritized zero-friction accessibility, human-centered interaction, and strict scientific verifiability. NASA’s combustion datasets span decades across separate archives, creating steep barriers for both engineers and learners; by ranking the 24 foundational research papers by relevance and enforcing mandatory primary-source citations in Curie, we ensure users immediately surface the most critical evidence free from generative hallucinations. Combining hands-free gesture controls, voice activation, and full multilingual support also makes complex orbital combustion physics intuitive across diverse backgrounds. Ultimately, FireGuard AI accelerates material screening, habitat atmosphere design, and early smoke-detection calibration for future Artemis lunar bases and deep-space missions, while empowering professors and students in chemistry, physics, mathematics, and aerospace engineering to explore real NASA flight science interactively.
